quarterly_data.quarter: Shin-Etsu Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Annual securities report, year to March 2026: ordinary profit JPY 708,281 million (-13.7%). Segments other than Electronics Materials: Infrastructure Materials (PVC, caustic soda) sales JPY 981,370 million (-5.8%), operating income JPY 164,890 million (-43.4%) - North American PVC demand was firm until mid-2025, then weakened and prices softened, prices stayed low in Asia and other overseas markets, and caustic soda price and volume were broadly stable; after raw-material and energy prices rose on the outbreak of war in Iran and the Middle East, the company began and pushed through price increases on all products. Functional Materials sales JPY 440,847 million (-1.7%), operating income JPY 100,955 million (+0.9%), as the focus on high-functionality products paid off. Processing, Trading & Specialized Services sales JPY 135,985 million (-0.5%), operating income JPY 27,338 million (-5.0%); demand for semiconductor-wafer containers was firm and silicone moulded products for automobiles grew. Sales by customer location: Japan JPY 549,936 million, United States JPY 705,099 million, other JPY 1,318,932 million. No single customer accounted for 10% or more of consolidated net sales.
quarterly_data.figure: Ordinary profit JPY 708,281 million (-13.7%); Infrastructure Materials OI JPY 164,890 million (-43.4%); US sales JPY 705,099 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Shin-Etsu Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capex and plan (annual securities report): capital expenditure in the year to March 2026 was JPY 339,706 million (including intangibles such as goodwill). Electronics Materials JPY 212,366 million - mainly quality upgrades and capacity additions for semiconductor silicon wafers at Shin-Etsu Handotai, and new and expanded semiconductor lithography-materials production facilities; Infrastructure Materials JPY 67,856 million (mainly the expansion of PVC raw-material facilities at Shintech); Functional Materials JPY 56,077 million (silicone capacity expansion and rationalisation); Processing, Trading & Specialized Services JPY 7,216 million. Capex plan (new and expansion) for the next year: JPY 350,000 million - Electronics Materials JPY 176,000 million (new facilities, expansion, rationalisation, maintenance), Infrastructure Materials JPY 122,000 million, Functional Materials JPY 42,000 million, Processing, Trading & Specialized Services JPY 10,000 million; the company states it does not fix project-by-project plans at year-end, so it discloses by segment. Main facilities at March 31, 2026 (book value): Isesaki plant (semiconductor lithography materials) JPY 54,444 million; Shin-Etsu Handotai Shirakawa plant (semiconductor silicon) JPY 104,702 million and Isobe plant JPY 74,219 million; Shin-Etsu Electronics Materials Taiwan photoresist plant JPY 34,869 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 339,706 million (Electronics Materials JPY 212,366 million); next-year plan JPY 350,000 million (Electronics Materials JPY 176,000 million)

quarterly_data.quarter: Shin-Etsu Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D (annual securities report): group R&D expense in the year to March 2026 was JPY 77,819 million; new-field work centres on semiconductor-related materials, high-speed communications, healthcare and materials for the SDGs and carbon neutrality. Photoresist: EUV resist and multilayer-material performance keeps being improved for device scaling; the 2nm generation has already moved to mass production, and development is now being strengthened mainly on EUV process materials for 1.4nm and beyond. EUV mask blanks have also entered mass production. The two Shin-Etsu Handotai laboratories develop leading-edge wafer technology for device scaling and next-generation thin-film SOI wafers and FZ wafers for lower power and higher speed. Optical-fiber preforms: active R&D in optical communications to keep world-top-level quality. Rare-earth magnets are adopted in hybrid cars and data-center hard-disk drives, where demand is expected to grow.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D JPY 77,819 million; 2nm resist in mass production; EUV materials for 1.4nm and beyond in development; EUV mask blanks in mass production

quarterly_data.quarter: Shin-Etsu Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management policy and outlook (annual securities report): management states its target indicators are higher sales and higher profit every year and that it will pursue further growth next year; it will expand its functions as a comprehensive maker of advanced electronic materials, especially those supporting the advance of AI, and pursue business opportunities in AI infrastructure in all business segments, while seeking economies of scale in Infrastructure Materials. It will constantly check its supply systems and take early steps to expand them to meet customer demand, and take multi-pronged measures against excessive exports from China, which it expects to continue in several markets for a considerable period. Management states it will invest actively with a medium- to long-term view so it can meet customer and market demand in time.
